name: Flat LAN, exposed services
reason: Direct network access to auxiliary services on the POS subnet without segmentation. Attacker can scan or probe ports directly.

name: LAN-path resource exhaustion
reason: Flooding the local broadcast domain or switch table causing denial of service to POS transactions.

name: Metadata exposure
reason: Passive sniffing of broadcast unencrypted broadcast metadata or mDNS/SSDP announcements; very low detectability.

name: ARP address resolution
reason: Gratuitous ARP poisoning or spoofing to divert terminal gateway traffic on the unsegmented LAN.

name: Certificate and name checks
reason: Improper validation of TLS root certs or hostname pinning during endpoint communication.

name: DHCP rogue server (Unauthenticated Network Configuration)
reason: Attacker injects rogue DHCP OFFER with malicious default gateway and DNS servers. Chosen as primary detection-phase research target due to high detectability (D=5) and feasibility (F=4), despite ranking 6th on risk.

name: Endpoint and update auth
reason: Firmware or application update mechanisms lacking strong cryptographic signature validation.

name: DNS lookup spoofing
reason: Responding to DNS queries with malicious host IPs before the legitimate resolver responds.

name: NTP time manipulation
reason: Manipulating system clock via unauthenticated NTP to invalidate or prematurely expire TLS certificates.

name: Message integrity and freshness
reason: Replaying captured POS authorization requests or responses when nonces/counters are absent.

name: Wi-Fi management frames (Deauth)
reason: Sending 802.11 deauthentication frames to kick the POS terminal off the authorized merchant BSSID.
